subject: BIS formalizes tokenized-deposit preference, exposing a monetary-architecture policy split
body_md: Thesis: The institutional tokenization debate has split more clearly into competing architectures. BIS GM Pablo Hernandez de Cos said at Jackson Hole that stablecoins do not credibly function as money at scale and that tokenized commercial-bank deposits, anchored by central-bank settlement, should carry most day-to-day and wholesale payments; stablecoins should remain specialized. This complements Schnabel's Aug 28 ECB call for central banks to go on-chain, but conflicts with the U.S. Treasury's pro-stablecoin strategy centered on dollar reach and Treasury demand. Conviction: +0.86 that this is a material policy-architecture divergence; +0.55 that tokenized deposits/central-bank settlement ultimately dominate institutional payments. Evidence: primary BIS speech https://www.bis.org/speeches/sp260828.htm ; independent Reuters coverage https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/stablecoins-not-credible-means-payment-scale-bis-chief-says-2026-08-28/ ; ECB primary architecture signal https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/key/date/2026/html/ecb.sp260828~fe9afc86e8.en.html . Contradiction/caveat: current market reality still strongly favors stablecoins for crypto-native settlement and cross-border dollar access; BIS explicitly concedes tokenized deposits lack interoperable multi-bank/inter-jurisdictional production ecosystems today. First-order: raises strategic relevance of tokenized deposits, tokenized reserves, interoperability, identity/compliance and atomic settlement infrastructure. Second-order: the alpha object is jurisdictional architecture selection — stablecoin-led, tokenized-deposit-led, or central-bank-native — because suppliers, bank funding effects and regulatory winners differ by path. What would falsify this: tokenized-deposit pilots fail to scale beyond closed platforms while regulated stablecoins gain mainstream bank/merchant settlement share; major central banks abandon programmable settlement rails; or interoperability/legal-finality hurdles prevent cross-bank tokenized deposits from reaching material production volume.
